note: Rewritten from the original English description by Sands (1959); the original is in English, the alate is described for the first time in that paper (recorded in the original as Previously undescribed), and the soldier section only adds the variation of the tooth and measurements (the original records that Silvestri's description had to be added); in the scan the head length entry reads "0-89-r- 18" (which should be 0.89—1.18) and has been restored from the column positions and the mean of 1.03; only the ranges are adopted for the measurements.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The variation of the mandibular tooth of the soldier is the greatest among the species of the genus in Africa: the tooth may range from a backward-directed state continuous with the inner margin in front of it to a projecting, erect, slightly forward-directed, obliquely truncate and acute state; the inner margin from the base of the tooth to the apex is a regular arc. The amplitude of this variation is established from numerous specimens from East and West Africa, and the type specimen lies near the reduced end of the series rather than at the extreme. The 15-segmented antennae belong to the alate, and the fore coxa of the soldier bears spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Colour: head and pronotum of the female deep sepia brown, postclypeus paler, yellowish brown; antennae brown, the apex of each segment yellowish white; labrum yellow; meso- and metanotal plates yellow, the remaining thoracic sclerites yellowish brown; abdominal tergites and the sides of the sternites sepia brown; legs: femora yellow, tibiae yellowish brown at the base and gradually paler towards the apex, tarsi yellow; middle of the abdominal sternites yellowish white; wings semi-transparent brown, the veins sepia brown. Posterior margin of the head almost semicircular; fontanelle smaller than an ocellus, very weakly concave, in front of it a very small pale extension, with a short, shallow, forked groove on each side; eye distinctly longer than the postclypeus; ocelli moderate, the distance to the eye about half the width of an ocellus; postclypeus inflated, about half as long as wide or slightly less, posterior margin convex, arched in the middle, sides fairly straight, anterior margin straight or slightly concave; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 about half of segment 2, segments 4 and 5 subequal, shorter than segment 2 and longer than segment 3. Pronotum distinctly narrower than the head width including eyes, anterior margin straight or slightly undulate, sides broadly rounded, narrowing posteriorly to a very shallowly emarginate posterior margin. Sclerite hairs pale; the hairs of the abdominal intersegmental membranes curved and pale yellow. Male similar to female, but the posterior part of the abdominal sternites evenly brown, the intersegmental hairs sparser and the wings slightly shorter. Measurements (mm): head width including eyes 0.89—0.91; maximum diameter of eye 0.22—0.23; ocelli 0.07—0.09 × 0.10—0.13; ocellus to eye 0.02—0.04; pronotum width 0.68—0.77, length 0.43—0.47; hind tibia length 0.82—0.93; forewing length 7.70—8.10.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Sands supplements Silvestri's original description: the mandibular tooth is highly variable, ranging from a backward-directed state continuous with the inner margin in front of it to a projecting, erect, slightly forward-directed, obliquely truncate and acute state; the inner margin from the base of the tooth to the apex is a regular arc. Measurements (mm): head length 0.89—1.18; maximum head width 0.74—0.91; head width at the mandible base 0.58—0.68; head thickness 0.61—0.72; left mandible length 0.61—0.72; pronotum length 0.29—0.32, width 0.47—0.54; hind tibia length 0.68—0.75.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The postclypeus is flatter than in A. acinacifer; the third marginal tooth of the left mandible has no clear boundary with the cutting edge between it and the first marginal tooth.
